9.1What a sound bank is

Strudel can only play sounds it knows by name. This part lists those names: the sound bank. There are four kinds of sound, and you write each kind a little differently:

KindWhat it isHow you write itPlays any note?List
Drum machineThe recorded drums of one machine (a TR-909, a LinnDrum…). Every machine uses the same short drum names: bd kick, sd snare, hh hi-hat…s("bd sd").bank("RolandTR909")No9.2, 9.3
SynthA sound wave made by the browser itself, so it loads instantlynote("a2").s("sawtooth")Yes9.4
InstrumentRecordings of a real instrument (piano, violin, choir…), played back at any pitchnote("c4").s("gm_violin")
note("c4").s("piano")		Yes9.5, 9.6
Sample setOther recordings: noises, voices, percussion from around the worlds("crow")Mostly no9.7

.bank() is only for drum machines. It adds the machine's name in front of each drum name: s("bd").bank("RolandTR909") plays the sound RolandTR909_bd. An instrument is a single name, so you write it in s(): s("piano"), never .bank("piano") (that looks for piano_bd, finds nothing and stays silent).

setcpm(100/4)

// drum machine: drum names + .bank()
$: s("bd*2 [~ bd] sd ~, hh*8").bank("RolandTR808")
// synth: a wave made in the browser
$: note("<a1 f1 c2 g1>").s("sawtooth").lpf(600).decay(.2).sustain(0)
// instrument: recordings of a piano, at any pitch
$: note("<[a3,c4,e4] [a3,c4,f4] [g3,c4,e4] [g3,b3,d4]>").s("piano").gain(.7)
// sample set: a crow, now and then
$: s("~ ~ ~ crow").gain(.4).mask("<0 1>")
CommandWhat it does
s("bd*2 [~ bd] sd ~, hh*8").bank("RolandTR808")A beat on the TR-808 drum machine: kick, snare and eight hi-hats. Change the bank name to hear the same beat on another machine.
note("<a1 f1 c2 g1>").s("sawtooth")A bass note per bar on the sawtooth synth wave. .lpf(600) darkens it, and .decay(.2).sustain(0) makes each note short.
note("<[a3,c4,e4] …>").s("piano")One chord per bar on the sampled grand piano. The commas mean the notes play together. .gain(.7) = 70 % volume.
s("~ ~ ~ crow").mask("<0 1>")A crow on beat 4, but only every second bar (0 = silent, 1 = play).

To find a sound by ear, open the sounds tab in Strudel: it lists every name, and clicking a name plays it. Which octave suits each instrument is in 3.1 Notes and octaves.

9.2Drum machines for .bank()

Every bank uses the same short drum names, so you can swap the kit by changing one word. A short alias works too: .bank("TR909") is the same as .bank("RolandTR909").

s("bd*2 [~ bd] sd ~, hh*8").bank("<RolandTR808 LinnDrum AkaiMPC60 CasioRZ1>")

This example plays a different drum machine each bar.

9.4Built-in synths

These are generated in the browser, so they load instantly and play any note. Use them with note() or n().scale(), and shape them with .lpf(), .attack(), .decay(), .sustain() and .release().

note("a2 c3 e3 g3").s("<sawtooth square triangle supersaw>").lpf(1200)

9.5Instruments (General MIDI)

128 sampled instruments, all named gm_…. They play any note and are good for chords and melodies. Always write the name in double quotes, .s("gm_choir_aahs"). Without quotes you get gm_choir_aahs is not defined (see Error messages).

note("<[a3,c4,e4] [f3,a3,c4] [c4,e4,g4] [g3,b3,d4]>")
  .s("gm_pad_warm").room(.6)

9.6Acoustic instruments (VCSL)

Real instruments from the Versilian Community Sample Library. Pitched ones play any note. Also listed here is piano, a large grand-piano sample set. Write it as an instrument, note("c4").s("piano"), not as a drum machine with .bank().

n("0 2 4 [7 6] 4 2").scale("C4:major").s("marimba")

You can also load the large Dirt-Samples library (about 200 folders of drums, noises and loops) from GitHub with one line at the top of your code. Each folder holds several recordings, and .n() picks one:

samples('github:tidalcycles/dirt-samples')

s("arpy*4").n("<0 2 4 6>")
